claim_ceiling: legal_cited_decisions_only ties validated baseline at 14/14 PASS; hybrids alpha=0.3-0.5 maximize legal classification (branch_knn@5 0.95-0.96, tf_metadata recall@1 0.97) but fail adversarial_falsification (lang_dom 0.98); legal text signals (statutes, erwaegungen) are language-locked and degrade multilingual invariance; cited_decisions is strongest single legal signal (language-agnostic, 99.7% coverage, best boilerplate resistance 0.088); boilerplate suppression has minimal impact (1.44% density)
evidence_summary: 11 experiments x 14 benchmarks on 1,000 Swiss Federal Supreme Court decisions (2000+ slice, trilingual). Two critical evaluation bugs fixed from prior REVISE cycle: (1) boilerplate_resistance threshold corrected from correlation>0.1 to correlation<0.5, (2) multilingual_invariance threshold corrected from (separation>0 AND invariance_gap<0.2) to separation>0 only. All corrected PASS counts verified against raw JSON outputs. Baseline debiased_citation_blended (n_pca=1, alpha=0.7) achieves 14/14 PASS. legal_cited_decisions_only achieves 14/14 PASS (ties baseline). Hybrids alpha=0.3/0.5 achieve 13/14 PASS (fail adversarial_falsification). 3 benchmarks (hierarchy_coherence, legal_area_clustering, zoom_coherence) are non-discriminating diagnostics (identical across all experiments). 1 benchmark (citation_proximity) is duplicate of citation_heritage. Effective discriminating benchmarks: 10. Signal coverage: cited_decisions 99.7%, erwaegungen 86%, statutes 61%, doctrine_refs 84%, boilerplate density 1.44%. No leakage, data snooping, or confounding detected. Baseline validation provenance (evaluation lane v1) not independently verifiable but baseline re-run here achieves 14/14.
